newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe refuses junior French minister's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Juppe refuses junior French minister's resignation.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Sunday refused the resignation of junior foreign minister Margie Sudre, who offered to step down after losing a by-election on the French Indian Ocean island of La Reunion.

Sudre, secretary of state for Francophonie, the club of French-speaking countries grouping 400 million people worldwide, was beaten by Communist Claude Hoarau in a run-off vote for election to the National Assembly by a 56-44 percent margin.
Conservative Juppe said he had spoken to both Sudre, 52, and to President Jacques Chirac after her defeat.

"In accord with the president, the prime minister has asked Madame Margie Sudre to continue her mission as secretary of state for Francophonie, where her efficient action is unanimously appreciated," Juppe said in a statement.
After conceding defeat to Hoarau, Sudre had said she was tendering her resignation to Juppe and Chirac. "We have lost a battle, we have not lost the war," she said.
Sudre, a doctor who was one of only four of 12 women in Juppe's cabinet to survive a reshuffle in November, had urged A massive turnout in Sunday's vote in a traditional Communist constituency.
Sudre won regional elections in 1993. Opponents say she has acted as a left-winger in La Reunion and a right-winger in Paris.

After the first by-election round open to all candidates a week ago, Hoarau was ahead with 47.6 percent to 42.5 percent for Sudre. Neither won half the vote, forcing the run-off. Sudre had said she would resign from the cabinet if beaten.
The seat fell vacant because Communist Paul Verges shifted to the Senate. It was Sudre's first attempt to win election to the National Assembly.

She was appointed to the cabinet when Juppe became prime minister in May 1995. In late 1994, Chirac met her in La Reunion during his campaign for the French presidency and kissed her hand, taken by many as the start of her rise into national politics.
Among her projects has been to challenge the domination of English on the Internet world computer network.
